question: Manish bought an electronic gadget with a 25% discount on the MRP. He made a profit of ₹600 by selling it for Rs. 18,600. The marked price of the electronic gadget was:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 18,600 and Profit = Rs. 600.

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Profit = 18,600 − 600 = Rs. 18,000.

Discount = 25%, so CP is 75% of the Marked Price (MRP).

75% of MRP = 18,000 ⇒ 3/4 × MRP = 18,000.

MRP = 18,000 × 4 ÷ 3 = 6,000 × 4 = Rs. 24,000.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 24,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** SP = Rs. 18,600, Profit = Rs. 600, Discount % = 25%.

**Formulas:** CP = SP − Profit | MRP = CP ÷ (1 − Discount%/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a294aef385ea764d445ecbabaf1d9104bd4a987ddb639f5392b8ff78dffd8628.png] 

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** of the gadget = Selling Price − Profit

⇒ CP = 18,600 − 600 = 18,000

⇒ Let **Marked Price (MRP)** be x.

⇒ Discounted price = x − 25% of x = 0.75x

⇒ Since Manish bought it at this price, 0.75x = 18,000

⇒ x = 18,000 ÷ 0.75 = 18,00,000 ÷ 75 = 24,000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 24,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

The price printed on an item is the **Marked Price (MRP)**. Discount is always calculated on the MRP to arrive at the **purchase price** for the buyer.

Profit and Loss

**Profit** occurs when the Selling Price is greater than the Cost Price. Profit = SP − CP. To find the CP when SP and Profit are known, we subtract Profit from SP.</p
